nodes.label: R18: Material changes
nodes.rationale: Proposal: a change is material at 10 percent on a budget line or 5 percent of the total budget, and on any date or venue change; the Project Manager approves it, and senior management too above 15 percent of the total. Options: agree / thresholds ___ / approval rule ___.

nodes.label: R19: Archiving
nodes.rationale: Proposal: a reminder before the three months end; the Project Manager proposes archiving and the Super Admin approves; afterwards the client sees only a contact route; reopening on request is read-only for 30 days. Options: agree / changes ___.

nodes.label: R2: Payment gateway
nodes.rationale: Proposal: Razorpay, unless AMPM already has a merchant account elsewhere. Options: agree / use ___.

nodes.label: R3: Refunds
nodes.rationale: The rule if a client wants the Rs 50,000 back. Proposal: no refund once the subscription is activated; full refund if AMPM cancels before activation. Options: agree / cooling-off period of ___ / case by case.

nodes.label: R4: Web as well as apps
nodes.norm_label: r4: web as well as apps
nodes.rationale: Whether clients also use hotel discovery and the wedding portal in a browser on a laptop. Proposal: yes, built from the same code as the client app; the team app stays native only. Flagged as the largest open cost item. Options: apps only / apps plus web (proposal) / web for clients, apps for the team.

nodes.label: R5: Representative logins
nodes.rationale: One shared login for the two family representatives or one account each. Proposal: one account per representative with the same rights on the same wedding, so every approval carries a name. Options: two accounts (proposal) / one shared login. One of the two CONFLICT points: the compiled answers say one shared login, the brief prefers separate accounts.

nodes.label: R6: Approvals
nodes.rationale: Whether one representative's approval completes a decision or both must approve. Proposal: one, with a setting to require both for budgets and contracts later. Options: one approval (proposal) / both for budgets and contracts / both for everything.

nodes.label: R7: Money the client sees
nodes.rationale: Proposal: planned and approved amounts per function, invoices issued to the client and their payment status; actual spend stays internal; never vendor quotes, costs or margins. Options: agree / approved amounts only / also actual spend and variance.

nodes.label: R8: Hotel services with a fee
nodes.norm_label: r8: hotel services with a fee
nodes.rationale: Availability checks are included in the subscription. Proposal: negotiation, site visits, contract review and booking assistance need a recorded service agreement first. Options: agree / all included in the subscription / fee only on ___.

nodes.label: R9: Staff roles and costs
nodes.rationale: Proposal: the nine roles from AMPM's specification; hotel costs visible to Super Admin, Finance, the Hotel Team and the Project Manager for their own weddings; vendor costs to Super Admin, Finance, the Vendor Coordinator and the Project Manager for their own weddings; nobody else. Options: agree / changes ___.

nodes.label: Small defaults
nodes.rationale: Eight unnumbered defaults collected at the foot of the sheet, each a tick or a blank: accounting export for AMPM's accountant (CSV, Tally, Zoho Books, other); website analytics and a bot check on the forms; who at AMPM signs each phase's acceptance; emergency reading of identity documents by the Super Admin, audited (allowed, two people, never); RSVP reminders then a call from the RSVP team with no guest edits after the deadline; readiness checklists hidden from the client; programme and calendar files to guests once invitations go out; one subscription per client account covering that client's weddings. Kept off the numbered list because none of them changes the shape of the build.

nodes.label: Data Platform and Identity: Options and Prices

nodes.label: Amazon Cognito (identity, recommended)
nodes.rationale: Usable from any host; 10,000 MAU free then US$0.015/user; custom SMS sender to a DLT provider via a Lambda; effectively free for AMPM for years.

nodes.label: Firebase Auth / Identity Platform
nodes.rationale: Phone OTP goes through Google SMS ~US$0.07/message to India and cannot use the DLT provider; wrong tool for mobile-OTP sign-in in India.

nodes.label: Option A: AWS as drafted
nodes.rationale: Full enterprise posture (two Indian regions, per-bucket KMS keys, WAF, rehearsed recovery); highest ops load and bill (US$450-900/mo at launch) but no redesign.

nodes.label: Option B: AWS lite growing into A
nodes.norm_label: option b: aws lite growing into a
nodes.rationale: Recommended before the VPS was known: same Terraform at a quarter of cost during build (US$180-250/mo), Multi-AZ and the Hyderabad copy switched on at launch with no migration; Cognito identity free.

nodes.label: Option C: Supabase Pro in Mumbai
nodes.norm_label: option c: supabase pro in mumbai
nodes.rationale: Least operations and bundled identity; gives up the second region and customer keys; the S3 Mumbai identity bucket hybrid restores the key that matters; recommended if AWS is unfamiliar (K4).

nodes.label: Option D: DigitalOcean in Bangalore
nodes.rationale: Simplest console and lowest bill with managed PostgreSQL PITR and a standby; no second region, no KMS; identity must come from Cognito or Supabase Auth.

nodes.label: Option E: Google Cloud in Mumbai
nodes.norm_label: option e: google cloud in mumbai
nodes.rationale: Equivalent posture with Delhi as a second region but a full infra redesign; Identity Platform phone OTP ~US$0.07/SMS so OTP stays in the API with MSG91.

nodes.label: Option F: Azure in Central India
nodes.norm_label: option f: azure in central india
nodes.rationale: Equivalent posture (Chennai as a second region) but a full infra redesign; right only if the developer already knows Azure.

nodes.label: Option G1: Hybrid VPS + managed data
nodes.norm_label: option g1: hybrid vps + managed data
nodes.rationale: VPS runs the application; PostgreSQL/PITR, S3 and Cognito managed elsewhere; the box rebuilt from Compose in an hour; cheapest sound build-time platform.

nodes.label: Option G2: Everything on the VPS (DECIDED)
nodes.norm_label: option g2: everything on the vps (decided)
nodes.rationale: Locked 26 Oct 2026: PostgreSQL, files (MinIO/S3) and an optional self-hosted IdP all on the box; cheapest by far and the most ways to lose data; the brief's security is met only if part 7.2 is done in full.

nodes.label: R13 hosting decision
nodes.rationale: Locked 26 Oct 2026 as G2 (dedicated VPS); the recommendation before the VPS was Option B, else C with the S3 identity hybrid; an Indian datacentre is a condition.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth (identity option)

nodes.rationale: guests references a missing family_groups table, guest_function_attendance is per guest yet carries party_count, and allocations and travel use a polymorphic guest/group id; rooming and identity handling need individuals while headcounts need groups including children, so the individual guest must be the atomic record and the family group a grouping.

nodes.rationale: The Aadhaar framework restricts private storage and use of Aadhaar numbers; recommended position is never to store them and, where hotels need identity for check-in, to keep only document type and a masked reference under restricted access with deletion after checkout.

nodes.rationale: The client's view of one enquiry with internal work excluded (SPEC 12 negotiation test): notes_internal, internal-only events, outcome_internal and internal_total_amount are absent from the response, not hidden (architecture 6). Milestone amounts only where W-14 applies.

nodes.label: Client portal: hotel discovery CP-01 to CP-11 (Phase 1)
nodes.norm_label: client portal: hotel discovery cp-01 to cp-11 (phase 1)
nodes.rationale: The subscription product: search, destinations, hotel detail with freshness labels, saved hotels and compare, request hotel assistance, enquiry tracking, proposal decisions, subscription and agreements.

nodes.label: TW-21 Hotels list
nodes.rationale: The private hotel database (BIZ 2.A: never public) with freshness filters and bulk demo visibility.

nodes.label: TW-22 Hotel profile editor
nodes.rationale: Verification per field group with next due; Preview as client renders CP-05 through the client serialiser and is the only way to see what clients see (architecture 6); media without rights cannot be set client or public (GP-20).

nodes.label: TW-23 Rate card editor
nodes.rationale: A card cannot be verified without a verification record; stale is set by the job, not by hand (GP-8, A-9).

nodes.label: TW-24 Verification queue
nodes.rationale: What needs re-checking by due date (SPEC 8 stale rule).

nodes.label: TW-25 Hotel import
nodes.rationale: Spreadsheet import of hotels, rooms, venues and rates (GP-22, RK-1); imported rates are unverified until a verification row exists.

nodes.label: Team workspace area: Hotels (TW-2x)
nodes.rationale: The flowchart's Database is the Hotels area (W-2, W-12); BIZ section 2.A: the hotel database is never public.

nodes.label: Freshness label on hotel commercial values
nodes.norm_label: freshness label on hotel commercial values
nodes.rationale: Every hotel commercial value carries Verified on <date> by AMPM, Stale, last checked <date>, or Rates on request (SPEC sections 8 and 12). Stale and unverified values never use the word confirmed; stale is set by a job, never by hand; a rate card cannot be verified without a verification record.

nodes.label: Client Portal — Hotel Discovery Screens (sign-in/activation, subscriber home, destinations, hotel search/filter, hotel detail with last-verified commercial information, compare and save, request assistance, track enquiry/negotiation/visit/proposal/booking status)
nodes.norm_label: client portal — hotel discovery screens (sign-in/activation, subscriber home, destinations, hotel search/filter, hotel detail with last-verified commercial information, compare and save, request assistance, track enquiry/negotiation/visit/proposal/booking status)

nodes.label: Module: Hotel Consultancy (availability enquiry, response, negotiation, site visit, proposal, booking milestone -> traceable hotel assistance)
nodes.norm_label: module: hotel consultancy (availability enquiry, response, negotiation, site visit, proposal, booking milestone -> traceable hotel assistance)

nodes.norm_label: module: hotel intelligence (destination, hotel, room category, inventory snapshot, venue, media, verification -> curated discovery with freshness labels)

nodes.label: Table: destinations (id, name, region, country, status; has many hotels)
nodes.norm_label: table: destinations (id, name, region, country, status; has many hotels)

nodes.label: Table: hotel_enquiries (id, account/project_id, hotel_id, dates, guest_count, status; responses, visits, proposals, negotiation events)
nodes.norm_label: table: hotel_enquiries (id, account/project_id, hotel_id, dates, guest_count, status; responses, visits, proposals, negotiation events)

nodes.norm_label: table: hotel_rooms / venues (id, hotel_id, category/type, capacity, facilities; may be proposed for a wedding)

nodes.label: Table: hotel_verifications (id, hotel_id, field_group, verified_at, source, status; freshness of price/facility information)
nodes.norm_label: table: hotel_verifications (id, hotel_id, field_group, verified_at, source, status; freshness of price/facility information)

nodes.norm_label: table: hotels (id, destination_id, profile, address, contact, status; rooms, venues, media, verification history)

nodes.label: Additional Hotel Services (Step 5: availability checks, price negotiation, site visits, contract review, booking assistance)
nodes.norm_label: additional hotel services (step 5: availability checks, price negotiation, site visits, contract review, booking assistance)
nodes.rationale: Treated according to the scope agreed with the client; separate from the discovery subscription.

nodes.label: Hotel Exploration (Step 4: location, venues/capacities, rooms, media, previous weddings, pricing/availability)
nodes.norm_label: hotel exploration (step 4: location, venues/capacities, rooms, media, previous weddings, pricing/availability)
nodes.rationale: The system should indicate whether prices and availability have been verified and when they were last checked.
nodes.source_file: reference_docs/AMPM Website & App —  Business Explanation for Developer.pdf

nodes.label: Q9 — Hotel data: EVA provides and updates ~3 times a year; venue/room/photos/menus/approximate package pricing shown as price ranges; availability checked only on request or cart add; photo rights controlled by AMPM
nodes.norm_label: q9 — hotel data: eva provides and updates ~3 times a year; venue/room/photos/menus/approximate package pricing shown as price ranges; availability checked only on request or cart add; photo rights controlled by ampm

nodes.label: Hotel Availability (no automated live calendar in the first release; request-based: client submits availability request or cart -> AMPM hotel team checks with the property -> records and shares response -> client compares; statuses indicative/requested/verified/awaiting confirmation)
nodes.norm_label: hotel availability (no automated live calendar in the first release; request-based: client submits availability request or cart -> ampm hotel team checks with the property -> records and shares response -> client compares; statuses indicative/requested/verified/awaiting confirmation)

nodes.label: Hotel Data Management (Eva maintains data and seasonal rates ~3 times a year; team can add/edit hotels, import from spreadsheets, update prices/packages, upload photos/menus, record verifier and date, mark outdated, manage media permissions)
nodes.norm_label: hotel data management (eva maintains data and seasonal rates ~3 times a year; team can add/edit hotels, import from spreadsheets, update prices/packages, upload photos/menus, record verifier and date, mark outdated, manage media permissions)
nodes.rationale: Previous clients' wedding photographs must not be published without appropriate permission.

nodes.label: Hotel Discovery Portal (paid, time-limited subscription for clients exploring wedding hotels)
nodes.norm_label: hotel discovery portal (paid, time-limited subscription for clients exploring wedding hotels)

nodes.label: Hotel Listing and Details (name/city/location, photos/videos, venues, room categories, approximate room/venue/package pricing, menu grid incl. veg/non-veg and per-plate, capacity, Street View/map, saved hotels, enquiry submission, availability-check requests, previous wedding photos only with permission)
nodes.norm_label: hotel listing and details (name/city/location, photos/videos, venues, room categories, approximate room/venue/package pricing, menu grid incl. veg/non-veg and per-plate, capacity, street view/map, saved hotels, enquiry submission, availability-check requests, previous wedding photos only with permission)
nodes.rationale: Purpose: help clients understand a hotel's suitability and approximate cost before proceeding with further discussions.

nodes.label: Pricing Rules (indicative prices and ranges, never internal cost or margin; vary by season, dates, guest count, room category; last-verified date; distinguish indicative pricing from confirmed quotations; availability not assumed from price; AMPM updates prices without code changes)
nodes.norm_label: pricing rules (indicative prices and ranges, never internal cost or margin; vary by season, dates, guest count, room category; last-verified date; distinguish indicative pricing from confirmed quotations; availability not assumed from price; ampm updates prices without code changes)

nodes.label: Rule 6 — Verify Changing Information
nodes.rationale: Hotel prices, availability and vendor availability can change; the system must make the verification status clear.
nodes.source_file: reference_docs/AMPM Website & App —  Business Explanation for Developer.pdf

nodes.label: Added requirement: adding a hotel to the selection or cart can trigger an availability request to the hotel team
nodes.norm_label: added requirement: adding a hotel to the selection or cart can trigger an availability request to the hotel team

nodes.label: Added requirement: hotel page content distinguishing indicative, requested, verified and awaiting-confirmation information
nodes.norm_label: added requirement: hotel page content distinguishing indicative, requested, verified and awaiting-confirmation information
nodes.rationale: Food and menu grid, vegetarian and non-vegetarian menus, approximate per-plate pricing, wedding package price ranges, indicative venue rental, approximate room pricing, street view or map.

nodes.label: Decision Q9: Eva maintains about 200 hotels with indicative price ranges verified about three times a year
nodes.norm_label: decision q9: eva maintains about 200 hotels with indicative price ranges verified about three times a year
nodes.rationale: Hotel pages show venue details, rooms, photos and videos, menu grid, approximate room pricing, wedding package ranges, indicative venue rental, approximate per-plate pricing, capacity, facilities and street view or map; prices are indicative ranges with a last-verified date, never internal cost; availability is checked by the team on request or when a hotel is added to a selection; previous clients' photographs only with permission; hotels importable from spreadsheets.

nodes.label: GP-20 Media rights for previous clients' wedding photos
nodes.norm_label: gp-20 media rights for previous clients' wedding photos
nodes.rationale: Hotel profiles will show other clients' wedding photos and videos but documents/media has only a visibility field and no consent or rights fields.

nodes.label: GP-22 Bulk import and migration
nodes.rationale: No document mentions import; AMPM presumably has hotel research in spreadsheets and clients supply guest lists in Excel, and the hotel import decides whether Phase 1 launches with a populated database.

nodes.label: GP-8 Hotel prices have nowhere to live
nodes.norm_label: gp-8 hotel prices have nowhere to live
nodes.rationale: BIZ and SPEC require quoted prices with verification dates but SPEC §4 has no price, rate, quote or snapshot entity; Indian wedding hotel commercials need room rates by category and season, venue rental, per-plate food-and-beverage minimums, taxes and inclusions, which call for a rate-card or quote-snapshot entity with its own verification record.

nodes.label: GP-9 Availability has no entity or calendar
nodes.norm_label: gp-9 availability has no entity or calendar
nodes.rationale: SPEC §12 says unverified availability is not shown as confirmed yet there is no availability entity; it should be stated as a per-enquiry manual check so the product does not promise live availability.

nodes.label: RK-1 Empty product at Phase 1 launch
nodes.norm_label: rk-1 empty product at phase 1 launch
nodes.rationale: Phase 1's value is a populated, verified hotel database, yet no document names a data source, data-entry plan, import tool or verification cadence; hotel data collection should start in parallel with design.

nodes.label: Brief section 2: hotels and prices
nodes.rationale: The specification's data model has no place to store a price or availability and previous clients' photos need permission. Default: rate cards by season with line items verified on a date by a named team member and shown as Stale after a set period; availability answered inside each enquiry, not a calendar; every photo and video carries a rights status; hotel data importable from spreadsheets.

nodes.label: Journey stage: hotel discovery and assistance (search, verified prices, enquiries, visits, proposals)
nodes.norm_label: journey stage: hotel discovery and assistance (search, verified prices, enquiries, visits, proposals)
nodes.rationale: Prices and verification are new: the specification had no price entity.

nodes.label: Assumed Q9: seasonal rate card with line items, availability answered per enquiry, media only with consent
nodes.norm_label: assumed q9: seasonal rate card with line items, availability answered per enquiry, media only with consent
nodes.rationale: The specification's data model had no place to put a price, so a rate card per season was designed with room rate per category, venue rental, per-plate minimums and taxes, each verified on a date by a named person; a live availability calendar would be a large addition; existing data imported from spreadsheets.
